# std/net.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from std/net.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

TCP sockets for programs on the hosted target (Linux and
the other targets whose native or C backend links the C library's socket
calls). Built on the `Host` capability, so a kernel or user program that
imports this file is rejected (`E-TARGET`). A call that fails (no such
listener, a closed descriptor, an address in use) gives `Option::None` or
`false`. On Windows the calls go to Winsock, loaded on the first call.

`import "std/net.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md).

| [`net_listen`](#net_listen) | Starts listening on `ip`:`port` (port 0 picks a free one). |
| [`net_port`](#net_port) | The port a listening socket is bound to. |
| [`net_connect`](#net_connect) | Connects to `ip`:`port`. |
| [`net_connect_timeout`](#net_connect_timeout) | Connects to `ip`:`port` within `ms` milliseconds (0 means no limit, as `net_connect`; more than an hour is cut to an hour). |
| [`net_connect6`](#net_connect6) | Connects over IPv6 to the 16-byte address `ip` (network order, as `dns_ip6` makes it) and `port`, giving up after `ms` milliseconds (as `net_connect_timeout`). |
| [`net_accept`](#net_accept) | Waits for a connection on a listening socket and returns it. |

| [`net_random`](#net_random) | `n` random bytes (at most 256) from the system's source (`/dev/urandom`, `RtlGenRandom`, `crypto.getRandomValues`), or `None` when there is none. |

```bastio
const NET_UDP_BROADCAST: u64 = 1;
```

Socket options for `net_udp_opt`: `NET_UDP_BROADCAST` (1 turns it on),
the unicast and multicast time to live (hop limit), multicast loopback,

## Functions

### `net_ip4`

```bastio
fn net_ip4(a: u64, b: u64, c: u64, d: u64) -> u64
```

An IPv4 address from its four parts, as `host_net` takes it.

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
if lo != 2130706433 { return 1; }
```

### `net_listen`

```bastio
fn net_listen(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Starts listening on `ip`:`port` (port 0 picks a free one).

Example:

```bastio
match net_listen(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => { net_close(host, s); },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `net_port`

```bastio
fn net_port(h: &Host, sock: u64) -> u64
```

The port a listening socket is bound to.

Example:

```bastio
match net_listen(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    net_close(host, s);
    if p == 0 { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `net_connect`

```bastio
fn net_connect(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Connects to `ip`:`port`.

Example:

```bastio
// Nothing listens on port 1.
match net_connect(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 1) {
  Option::Some(s) => { net_close(host, s); return 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
```

### `net_connect_timeout`

```bastio
fn net_connect_timeout(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64, ms: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Connects to `ip`:`port` within `ms` milliseconds (0 means no limit, as
`net_connect`; more than an hour is cut to an hour). The socket has the
same limit on every later read and write, so `net_recv` gives `None` when
nothing arrives in time and `net_send_all` returns false. The limit is not
applied on Windows yet: there the call blocks as `net_connect` does.

Example:

```bastio
// Nothing listens on port 1; the refusal comes at once.
match net_connect_timeout(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 1, 2000) {
  Option::Some(s) => { net_close(host, s); return 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
// A listener that is there: the connection is made and works.
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(l) => {
    match net_connect_timeout(host, lo, net_port(host, l), 2000) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, l) {
          Option::Some(a) => {
            let msg = bfrom("ping");
            let sent = net_send_all(host, c, msg);
            bfree(msg);
            let mut got = balloc(0);
            match net_recv(host, a, 16, &mut got) {
              Option::Some(n) => { if sent && n == 4 { bad = 0; } },
              Option::None => {},
            }
            bfree(got);
            net_close(host, a);
          },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, l);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `net_connect6`

```bastio
fn net_connect6(h: &Host, ip: &Bytes, port: u64, ms: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Connects over IPv6 to the 16-byte address `ip` (network order, as
`dns_ip6` makes it) and `port`, giving up after `ms` milliseconds (as
`net_connect_timeout`). `None` if `ip` is not 16 bytes, the host has no
IPv6, or the connection fails.

Example:

```bastio
// An address that nothing answers on port 1 (or a host with no IPv6):
// either way the connection fails.
let lo = bfrom("0123456789abcdef");
let mut bad = 0;
match net_connect6(host, lo, 1, 1000) {
  Option::Some(c) => { net_close(host, c); bad = 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(lo);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `net_accept`

```bastio
fn net_accept(h: &Host, sock: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Waits for a connection on a listening socket and returns it.

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, s) {
          Option::Some(a) => { bad = 0; net_close(host, a); },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `net_recv`

```bastio
fn net_recv(h: &Host, sock: u64, max: u64, out: &mut Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

Reads up to `max` bytes into `out` (replacing it). `Some(0)` is the end of
the stream.

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, s) {
          Option::Some(a) => {
            let msg = bfrom("hello");
            let sent = net_send_all(host, c, msg);
            bfree(msg);
            let mut got = balloc(0);
            match net_recv(host, a, 16, &mut got) {
              Option::Some(n) => { if sent && n == 5 { bad = 0; } },
              Option::None => {},
            }
            bfree(got);
            net_close(host, a);
          },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `net_send_all`

```bastio
fn net_send_all(h: &Host, sock: u64, data: &Bytes) -> bool
```

Sends all of `data`, retrying after a partial write. False if the
connection fails first.

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
match net_connect(host, lo, 1) {
  Option::Some(c) => { net_close(host, c); return 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
```

### `net_close`

```bastio
fn net_close(h: &Host, sock: u64)
```

Closes a socket.

Example:

```bastio
match net_listen(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => { net_close(host, s); },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `net_shutdown_send`

```bastio
fn net_shutdown_send(h: &Host, sock: u64) -> bool
```

Shuts down the sending direction of a connected socket: the peer reads
the end of the stream once it has read what was sent, while this side can
still receive. False if `sock` is not a connected socket, and on the
native backends, which do not have the call yet (the C backend does).

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    match net_connect(host, lo, net_port(host, s)) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, s) {
          Option::Some(a) => {
            let msg = bfrom("bye");
            let sent = net_send_all(host, c, msg);
            bfree(msg);
            if net_shutdown_send(host, c) {
              // The peer reads the message, then the end of the stream ...
              let mut got = balloc(0);
              let mut n1 = 0;
              let mut n2 = 1;
              match net_recv(host, a, 16, &mut got) { Option::Some(n) => { n1 = n; }, Option::None => {}, }
              match net_recv(host, a, 16, &mut got) { Option::Some(n) => { n2 = n; }, Option::None => {}, }
              // ... and can still answer.
              let ans = bfrom("ok");
              let back = net_send_all(host, a, ans);
              bfree(ans);
              let mut n3 = 0;
              match net_recv(host, c, 16, &mut got) { Option::Some(n) => { n3 = n; }, Option::None => {}, }
              bfree(got);
              if sent && back && n1 == 3 && n2 == 0 && n3 == 2 { bad = 0; }
            } else {
              bad = 0;
            }
            net_close(host, a);
          },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `net_connect_start`

```bastio
fn net_connect_start(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Starts a connection to `ip`:`port` without waiting for it: the socket
that comes back is non-blocking and the connection is under way. Wait
until the socket can be written to (`host_sys` operation 50, `os_poll`),
then ask `net_connect_result`. `None` when the socket cannot be made, and
on targets without this call (only the Linux C backend has it).

Example:

```bastio
// The socket is made at once, whatever the answer will be; a listener
// that is there accepts the connection.
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(l) => {
    match net_connect_start(host, lo, net_port(host, l)) {
      Option::Some(c) => { net_close(host, c); },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, l);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
```

### `net_connect_result`

```bastio
fn net_connect_result(h: &Host, sock: u64) -> u64
```

The outcome of a connection started with `net_connect_start`, once the
socket is writable: 0 when it is connected, else the system's error
number (111, refused, on Linux). 2^64 - 1 if `sock` cannot be asked.
Before the socket is writable the answer is 0 too, so wait first.

Example:

```bastio
// A descriptor that is not a socket cannot be asked.
if net_connect_result(host, 99999) != 18446744073709551615 { return 1; }
```

### `net_now`

```bastio
fn net_now(h: &Host) -> u64
```

The time in seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC, from the system clock (0 if
there is none). The caller of the TLS client gives this as `now`.

Example:

```bastio
// After 2023, and the clock does not run backwards.
let a = net_now(host);
let b = net_now(host);
if a < 1700000000 || b < a { return 1; }
```

### `net_random`

```bastio
fn net_random(h: &Host, n: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == n
```

`n` random bytes (at most 256) from the system's source (`/dev/urandom`,
`RtlGenRandom`, `crypto.getRandomValues`), or `None` when there is none.
The Bytes returned has exactly `n` bytes.

Example:

```bastio
match net_random(host, 32) {
  Option::Some(a) => {
    match net_random(host, 32) {
      Option::Some(b) => {
        // Two draws of 256 bits are the same with probability 2^-256.
        let same = bytes_eq(a, b);
        bfree(b);
        bfree(a);
        if same { return 1; }
      },
      Option::None => { bfree(a); return 1; },
    }
  },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `net_udp_open`

```bastio
fn net_udp_open(h: &Host, v6: bool) -> Option[u64]
```

A UDP socket (IPv6 when `v6`), not yet bound.

Example:

```bastio
match net_udp_open(host, false) {
  Option::Some(s) => { net_close(host, s); },
  Option::None => {},   // (no UDP on this backend or platform)
}
```

### `net_udp_bind`

```bastio
fn net_udp_bind(h: &Host, sock: u64, ip: &Bytes, port: u64, reuse: bool) -> bool
```

Binds `sock` to `ip`:`port` (port 0: any free port, which `net_sockname`
then gives). `reuse` sets SO_REUSEADDR first.

Example:

```bastio
match net_udp_open(host, false) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let mut ip = balloc(4);
    bset(&mut ip, 0, 127); bset(&mut ip, 1, 0); bset(&mut ip, 2, 0); bset(&mut ip, 3, 1);
    let ok = net_udp_bind(host, s, ip, 0, false);
    bfree(ip);
    net_close(host, s);
    if !ok { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => {},   // (no UDP on this backend or platform)
}
```

### `net_udp_send`

```bastio
fn net_udp_send(h: &Host, sock: u64, ip: &Bytes, port: u64, data: &Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

Sends `data` as one datagram to `ip`:`port`. The count sent, or `None`
(also when the send buffer is full: see `net_udp_again`).

Example:

```bastio
match net_udp_open(host, false) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let mut ip = balloc(4);
    bset(&mut ip, 0, 127); bset(&mut ip, 1, 0); bset(&mut ip, 2, 0); bset(&mut ip, 3, 1);
    let d = bfrom("hi");
    let r = net_udp_send(host, s, ip, 9, d);
    bfree(d); bfree(ip);
    net_close(host, s);
    if r is Option::None { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => {},   // (no UDP on this backend or platform)
}
```

### `net_udp_recv`

```bastio
fn net_udp_recv(h: &Host, sock: u64, max: u64, out: &mut Bytes, from_ip: &mut Bytes, from_port: &mut u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Receives one datagram of at most `max` bytes (a longer one is cut) into
`out`, with the sender's address in `from_ip` and its port in `from_port`.
`None` when there is none yet (`net_udp_again` is true) or on an error.

Example:

```bastio
match net_udp_open(host, false) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let mut out = balloc(0);
    let mut ip = balloc(0);
    let mut port = 0;
    let r = net_udp_recv(host, s, 100, &mut out, &mut ip, &mut port);
    bfree(out); bfree(ip);
    net_close(host, s);
    if r is Option::Some { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => {},   // (no UDP on this backend or platform)
}
```

### `net_udp_again`

```bastio
fn net_udp_again(h: &Host) -> bool
```

True when the last failed UDP call only meant "not now" (EAGAIN or
EWOULDBLOCK), as opposed to a real error.

Example:

```bastio
let again = net_udp_again(host);
if again { return 1; }
```

### `net_udp_opt`

```bastio
fn net_udp_opt(h: &Host, sock: u64, opt: u64, val: u64) -> bool
```

Sets option `opt` (one of the `NET_UDP_*` numbers) to `val`.

Example:

```bastio
match net_udp_open(host, false) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let ok = net_udp_opt(host, s, NET_UDP_BROADCAST, 1);
    net_close(host, s);
    if !ok { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => {},   // (no UDP on this backend or platform)
}
```

### `net_udp_getopt`

```bastio
fn net_udp_getopt(h: &Host, sock: u64, opt: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

The value of option `opt` (Linux reports twice the buffer sizes it was given).

Example:

```bastio
match net_udp_open(host, false) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let v = net_udp_getopt(host, s, NET_UDP_RCVBUF);
    net_close(host, s);
    if v is Option::None { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => {},   // (no UDP on this backend or platform)
}
```

### `net_udp_membership`

```bastio
fn net_udp_membership(h: &Host, sock: u64, group: &Bytes, iface: &Bytes, join: bool) -> bool
```

Joins (`join`) or leaves the IPv4 multicast `group` (4 bytes) on the
interface with address `iface` (4 bytes; all zero: the system's choice).

Example:

```bastio
match net_udp_open(host, false) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let g = balloc(3);
    let i = balloc(4);
    let ok = net_udp_membership(host, s, g, i, true);
    bfree(g); bfree(i);
    net_close(host, s);
    if ok { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => {},   // (no UDP on this backend or platform)
}
```

### `net_sockname`

```bastio
fn net_sockname(h: &Host, sock: u64, ip: &mut Bytes, port: &mut u64) -> bool
```

The local address and port of `sock` (a generalised `net_port`).

Example:

```bastio
match net_udp_open(host, false) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let mut ip = balloc(0);
    let mut port = 0;
    let ok = net_sockname(host, s, &mut ip, &mut port);
    bfree(ip);
    net_close(host, s);
    if !ok { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => {},   // (no UDP on this backend or platform)
}
```
